response.rationale: R4 best fits the non-progressive, unrevealing objective workup: normal VEP and ERG, unremarkable neuro-ophthalmologic testing, and normal neuroimaging exclude structural/traumatic causes; the raw referral span directly names the diagnostic suspicion, while organic candidates R1, R3, and C1 leave the redefinitive contradictions unexplained. R4 is favored because conversion disorder comcomposites the entire clinical picture.

rejected.why: Repeated completion derived from R3; retains the same contradiction of normal VEP and does not independently support bilateral optic neuropathy.
Strong diagnosis of traumatic optic neuropathy is undermined by normal visual evoked potentials and normal ophthalmic examination.
Concussion is mechanism/etc ambiguous, and the complete absence of CT/MRI lesionly qualification deficits makes TBI an insufficient diagnosis.
Commotio retinae is a reasonable trauma-linked contender but is unsupported when anterior and posterior segments are normal and ERG shows no retinal pathology.
